from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex waveforms emerge from simple rotating circles.",
            "Each circle acts as a basic rotating phasor.",
            "Combining different frequencies creates complex paths.",
            "This is the core of epicycles.",
            "Motion blends into a single smooth curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: Epicycles and Circular Motion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Animation Elements
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        
        point_p = Dot(circle.point_from_proportion(0), color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Track rotation
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_point(m):
            angle = tracker.get_value()
            m.move_to(circle.point_from_proportion(angle % 1))
            
        point_p.add_updater(update_point)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(circle), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(point_p), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF8000"), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=1)
        
        point_p.remove_updater(update_point)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Euler's formula connects circles to complex waves.", "Rotation projected creates simple sine waves.", "These waves form the basis of signals."]
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge: From Circles to Sine/Cosine Waves", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'B2')
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(circle.get_right())
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.get_center() + 0.8 * RIGHT * np.cos(tracker.get_value()) + 0.8 * UP * np.sin(tracker.get_value())))
        
        graph = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=3, y_length=2)
        self.place_at_grid(graph, 'B5')
        
        sine_curve = always_redraw(lambda: graph.plot(lambda x: 0.8 * np.sin(x + tracker.get_value()), x_range=[0, tracker.get_value() % 4], color="#00FFFF"))
        
        dashed_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(start=dot.get_center(), end=graph.c2p(0, 0.8 * np.sin(tracker.get_value()))))
        
        self.add(circle, dot, graph, sine_curve, dashed_line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#90EE90"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Fourier series model how heat diffuses.", "Sharp temperature details decay very quickly.", "Gradual heat patterns persist much longer."]
        self.setup_layout("The Heat Equation: Solving for Diffusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initial Mobjects
        rod = Line(start=LEFT*2.5, end=RIGHT*2.5, color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6)
        self.place_at_grid(rod, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Heat function (Gaussian)
        def heat_func(x, t):
            # Simple diffusion decay model
            sigma = np.sqrt(0.1 + t)
            return 1.5 * np.exp(-x**2 / (2 * sigma**2))

        self.t = ValueTracker(0)
        curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(lambda x: heat_func(x, self.t.get_value()), color=BLUE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(rod), FadeIn(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.play(self.t.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(self.t.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Circular Connection to Physics", [
            "The heat equation uses these circular basis.",
            "Harmonics describe temperature states over time.",
            "Cycles explain physical cooling perfectly."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "B2")
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(circle.point_from_proportion((self.time * 0.5) % 1)))
        
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t), x_range=[0, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, "D4")
        
        # Initialize elements
        self.add(circle, dot)
        self.add(wave)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87CEEB")) # Light sky blue
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32")) # Lime green
        mapping_line = Line(circle.get_right(), wave.get_start(), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(mapping_line))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500")) # Orange red
        equation = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha \nabla^2 u", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "F4")
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: From Circles to Heat: The Magic of Fourier Series

sections.title: The Intuition: Epicycles and Circular Motion
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any periodic waveform can be constructed by summing circular motions (phasors) of different frequencies and radii, visually represented as 'rotating gears' (epicycles).
sections.example: An animation of a robotic arm drawing a complex shape by adding the movements of several concentric rotating circles.

sections.title: The Bridge: From Circles to Sine/Cosine Waves
sections.content: Explain Euler's formula and how uniform circular motion projected onto a 2D plane creates the building blocks of Fourier Series: simple sine and cosine waves. Establish these as the 'musical notes' of a function.
sections.example: Visualizing a shadow cast by a rotating marble on a wall to show how circular rotation creates a perfect sine wave.

sections.title: The Heat Equation: Solving for Diffusion
sections.content: Apply Fourier series to the Heat Equation. Show that heat distribution is essentially a 'smoothing out' process, where each Fourier component (harmonic) decays at a specific rate over time.
sections.example: A metal rod with a dragon-shaped temperature profile; watch as the 'sharp' details (high-frequency harmonics) fade faster than the overall shape (low-frequency base).

sections.title: Synthesis: The Circular Connection to Physics
sections.content: Conclude by showing that the Heat Equation is separable into these same sine/cosine components. The circular nature of the wave basis allows us to predict the temperature state of any object at any future time.
sections.example: A circular pizza cooling down: showing the temperature diffusion using the 'radial' harmonics of a circle.
